summary: Backend + frontend regression for the 5-feature session (choreographer follows, chat @mentions, refresh recommendations, auto-hide/report+block, login title). Backend: 12/12 pytest cases pass in test_follow_mentions_refresh.py. Frontend: login gradient renders, all 3 new profile rows exist, choreographer discover list + follow bell works, dance detail shows follow pill next to 'By choreographer', admin refresh-recommendations screen loads with tabs + Rerun button, chat @mentions autocomplete triggers and shows Erin Brown for '@er'. Report+block sheet code (ReportFeedSheet) verified via code review — long-press could not be automated via web-preview Playwright but the 'Also block this user?' toggle + chained blockUser call are implemented (testID `report-also-block-toggle`).

critical.issue: CRITICAL: `feed_reactions.create_index('event_id')` (line 80) conflicts with an existing `event_id_1` unique index → raises IndexKeySpecsConflict inside the OUTER try/except and short-circuits all remaining index creates in the same block. As a result: `choreographer_follows`, `chat_mentions`, and `dance_drift_flags` NEVER get their unique indexes created. Confirmed via `db.<collection>.index_information()` — only the `_id_` index exists. Impact: (a) duplicate follow rows are possible when repeat POSTs land before the previous doc's read-modify-write completes; empirically reproduced — one Erin/Rob-Fowler pair produced 2 rows and my_follows returned duplicates; (b) mention ledger + drift-flag idempotency guarantees are not enforced. Fix: wrap each ensure_indexes() call in its own try/except so one collection's stale index doesn't stop the batch.

critical_code_review_comments: services/startup.py: too-broad try/except around ALL index creates masks failures. Per-collection try/except or a small `_safe_index_create(coll, spec)` helper would prevent one collection's failure from blocking the rest.

rca_of_issue: ROOT CAUSE (missing unique indexes on choreographer_follows / chat_mentions / dance_drift_flags): In `services/startup.py::_ensure_indexes` (lines 27-121) all `create_index` calls are wrapped in a single outer try/except. Line 80 attempts `db.feed_reactions.create_index('event_id')` which conflicts with a pre-existing unique index of the same name → raises `IndexKeySpecsConflict` → jumps to the shared `except Exception` at line 120 → the three NEW ensure_indexes() calls (choreographer, mentions, drift) at lines 106-119 are SKIPPED. REPRO: `python3 -c "from motor... db.choreographer_follows.index_information()"` shows only `_id_`. MITIGATION: (1) either give the feed_reactions index the same `unique=True` flag as the existing one, OR change to `create_index('event_id', name='by_event_id')` so it doesn't collide by name; and (2) wrap each ensure_indexes() call in its own try/except so a stale index earlier in the batch can never block later collections. After the fix, drop `_id_`-only state on prod is fine; the new create_index calls are idempotent. Also add a `db.choreographer_follows.delete_many({...})` + upsert migration to compact any historic duplicates before enabling the unique index (otherwise index creation will fail on the dupes).
